question:
When is the following arranged in ascending order which comes fourth?

(2)/(5),(3)/(5),(6)/(7),(1)/(3),(5)/(6)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert the given fractions into percentages for quick comparison:

2/5 = 40%, 3/5 = 60%, 6/7 ≈ 85.7%, 1/3 ≈ 33.3%, 5/6 ≈ 83.3%

Arranging the percentages in ascending order: 33.3% [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Fractions: 2/5, 3/5, 6/7, 1/3, 5/6

**Method Used:**

Convert each fraction into a decimal value to accurately compare and arrange them.

**Calculations:**

⇒ 1/3 ≈ 0.333

⇒ 2/5 = 0.400

⇒ 3/5 = 0.600

⇒ 5/6 ≈ 0.833

⇒ 6/7 ≈ 0.857

⇒ Arranging in ascending order (smallest to largest):

⇒ 0.333 
 
 1st: 1/3
 0.333

 
 2nd: 2/5
 0.400

 
 3rd: 3/5
 0.600

 
 4th: 5/6
 0.833

 
 5th: 6/7
 0.857

⇒ The fraction at the fourth position is 5/6.

**∴ The correct answer is 5/6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cross-Multiplication Method

To compare two fractions a/b and c/d, cross-multiply to get a×d and b×c. If a×d > b×c, then a/b > c/d.

Common Denominator Method (LCM)

Find the LCM of all denominators and convert each fraction into an equivalent fraction. The fraction with the largest numerator is the greatest.

Proper vs Improper Fractions

A proper fraction has a numerator smaller than its denominator (value < 1), while an improper fraction has a numerator greater than or equal to its denominator (value ≥ 1).
